issues.issue: The effective date is left as a blank line, so the instrument does not state when it takes effect.

Section 2.15 defines 'Effective Date' as 'the date first stated above', but the preamble states no date, leaving every deadline keyed to the Effective Date (4.1.10, 4.9.4, 10.3.3) without a starting point.

This recital describes the MTC Network as 'currently planned' with approximate figures, which could be set against the operative definition in Section 2.38 and the Commencement Date test in Section 2.8.
This recital of the Operator's skill could be set against the operative warranties in Section 5.1.6 and 5.1.7, but they point the same way.
The recital lists services 'among other things', a general catch-all against enumerated specifics whose reach is not fixed.
This recital's description of services could be argued against the operative scope of 'Services' in Section 2.60 and Article 4.
'functions, responsibilities and tasks ... otherwise commonly performed by a dark fiber and lit network provider' is an open-ended standard with no fixed boundary.
This recital's open-ended scope sits against Section 4.7.1, which sweeps unlisted tasks into the Services, and could be used to expand or limit Article 4 obligations.

The rule that all capitalized terms are defined in Article 2 is contradicted by capitalized terms used but never defined there, such as 'Applicable Third Party' (7.3.2, 7.5), 'Governmental Authority' (7.3, 7.5), 'Attachment Database' (4.3.4) and 'CAPEX Upgrade and Update Fund' (4.6.1).
Section 11.1.3 refers repeatedly to 'the Rules' rather than the defined 'AAA Rules', but the reference is readily harmonised.
'Control' is used to define 'Affiliate' without any ownership or voting threshold, leaving the boundary of the term uncertain.
Section 8.1.4 supplies a 50% voting-securities test for 'change of control' while this definition supplies none, so 'control' bears two possible measures in one instrument.
'the initial four empty conduit' and 'for any purpose consistent with the uses granted' leave the scope of qualifying alterations imprecise.
The definition cross-refers to Section 4.9.2, which governs agreements between MTC and third parties; the Annual Plan is actually required by Section 4.9.3.2.
The cross-reference cannot be reconciled with Section 4.9.3.2, which is the provision that actually requires the Annual Plan.
The list of CAIs may be revised 'in MTC's sole discretion up until the Commencement Date', but the term's content after that date is not addressed.
The CAI count drives the Commencement Date test in Section 2.8 and the payment reduction in Section 4.9.2.8, so unilateral revision of Exhibit A moves those triggers.
Limb (a) requires both 90% of mileage 'the Design-Build Contractor is engaged to construct' and 90% of CAIs connected, and the denominator for each is not fixed.
Section 4.9.2.8 assumes clause (a) may not occur until after thirty months even though clause (b) makes thirty months itself a Commencement Date, so the two provisions pull against each other.

'would reasonably be understood by the Parties, to be proprietary or confidential' plus a non-exhaustive list ('may include, but is not necessarily limited to') leaves the boundary of protected information uncertain.
The definition makes information of either Party confidential, while Section 7.3.4 declares all written materials containing Confidential Information the sole property of MTC.

A Dark Fiber Customer is defined as leasing 'from MTC', but Section 4.7.4.4 has the Network Operator execute extension leases in its own name and Section 4.7.4.5 splits payments received by the Operator.

The definition points to 'the date first stated above', but the preamble leaves the date blank, so the Effective Date on which Sections 4.1.10, 4.9.4 and 10.3.3 all depend is not ascertainable from the instrument.
'any financial statements of Network Operator delivered to MTC' is circular, defining the term by the act of delivery rather than by content.
'or other similar casualty, or other substantial and extraordinary accidents' is a general catch-all following a long enumerated list, raising an ejusdem generis question about its reach.
The definition contemplates 'mediation, arbitration, legal and/or administrative action', which sits against Article 11's requirement that all disputes go to arbitration.
Indemnified Parties include non-signatories such as Affiliates and successors, which sits against Section 12.11's statement that no rights are conferred on non-parties.
'the Party from which another person seeks or is entitled to indemnification' is drafted so that a mere unfounded demand makes a Party an Indemnifying Party.
'any of the rating factors used to measure performance ... in critical areas' is entirely circular and identifies no fixed set of indicators.
KPIs are to be in Exhibit E per the exhibit list and Section 4.13.1, but that SLA was unfinished at signing, so the measures against which performance is judged were not fixed.
'funded in whole or in part by MTC' gives no minimum share, so an extension with token MTC funding qualifies.
Section 4.5.7 provides that MTC owns any MBI Network Extension 'regardless of the source of its funding', which cannot be squared with a definition that requires MTC funding.

The definition mixes an operative statement ('as built or acquired ... including any MBI Network Extensions and IRUs') with descriptive planning figures ('currently planned as a 1,338-mile'), leaving the actual boundary of the asset uncertain.

Section 2.39 says a fiber extension becomes part of the MTC Network unless it is a Network Extension and the Operator proves otherwise, which pulls against a definition fixed at what was 'built or acquired by the MassBroadband 123 Project'.

The second sentence is circular: an extension becomes part of the MTC Network unless it is a Network Extension and the Operator establishes 'that it is not or does not become part of the MTC Network', so the test defines itself.
This default cannot be squared with Section 4.5.5, which makes Network Operator Network Extensions 'the sole property of the Network Operator'.
The definition captures only Axia NGNetworks USA, Inc., while Section 9.1 extends 'Network Operator' to subcontractors and assignees for indemnity purposes.
The heading of Section 3.6 speaks of rights 'Upon Termination or Expiration', but Section 3.6.1 grants them only 'upon expiration of the Term'.
'funded and owned by the Network Operator but excludes any Network Extension funded by MTC' does not say what happens to an extension funded jointly.
Section 2.36 defines MBI Network Extensions as those funded 'in whole or in part' by MTC, so a partly-Operator-funded extension can answer both definitions.
'similar services on the MTC Network' fixes the deemed fee by reference to an undefined comparison, and the illustrative example does not resolve which services are similar.
Section 2.45 includes deemed Extension Fees in Network Revenue while excluding '(z) services on Network Operator Network Extensions', so the same activity is both counted and excluded.
'plus any additional policies reasonably required by MTC to meet legal requirements' allows MTC to expand the set of binding policies unilaterally, and 'At present this is includes' is ungrammatical.
Section 4.12 requires 'full compliance with all Network Policies' even though the set can grow by MTC's later action under this definition.

The sweeping catch-all — 'Any amounts earned ... from services related to the MTC Network, other than the categories expressly excluded ... shall be Network Revenue' — sits against a specific enumerated list of inclusions and exclusions, so the reach of the general words is contestable.

Limb (b) includes deemed Network Operator Network Extension Fees while exclusion (z) excludes 'services on Network Operator Network Extensions', an inconsistency that also drives the revenue-share calculation under Section 4.9.5.
After construction, a Network Segment exists only 'by mutual agreement', so no Segment can be defined if the Parties disagree.
Section 3.6.1.5(b) prices dark fiber by 'the highest number of strands leased in any Network Segment', a calculation that depends on agreement that may never be reached.
'the contents of which shall be binding upon the entity' is unusual and does not say what legal consequence follows from a certificate later shown to be inaccurate.
Because 'Party' is limited to MTC and the Network Operator, Article 11's arbitration of disputes 'between the Parties' does not obviously reach the parent guarantor required by Section 12.14.
The definition places the Price Caps in Exhibit F, but the Agreement's exhibit list assigns Price Caps to Exhibit D and Exhibit F to the Master Services Agreement with EOPSS and ITD.
'additional custom quotations for non-standard customer requests' and prices set 'in its sole discretion' for extension customers leave the boundary between regulated and unregulated pricing unclear.
The carve-out for extension customers conflicts with Section 4.7.2, which caps all Wholesale Service rates at the Price Caps regardless of where the customer connects.
'Renewal Decision' is defined by reference to requirements in Section 3.2, but Section 3.2 contains no decision requirements and the defined term is never used elsewhere in the Agreement.
Sections 3.6.1.2, 3.6.1.3 and 3.6.1.4 all speak of a 'Request for Renewal' rather than the defined 'Renewal Request', leaving it arguable whether the same instrument is meant.
Defining 'Retail Service' as 'services provided by a Third Party Service Provider' is circular and identifies the service by its provider rather than its character.

Because Section 2.64 defines a Third Party Service Provider as any organization 'other than Network Operator', Section 4.8's prohibition on the Operator providing Retail Services is definitionally impossible.
'routine scheduled maintenance ... as described herein' is defined by reference to itself and to an inclusive example.
'all performance obligations of the Network Operator hereunder' is a wholly general definition with no boundary of its own.
Section 4.7.1 further sweeps in tasks 'whether or not specifically described in this Agreement', so the scope of Services is set by an implication test rather than by this definition.
The SLA to be attached as Exhibit E was, per Section 4.13.1, still being negotiated at signing, so the standards this definition presupposes did not exist.

Section 8.4.1 says the Term shall not 'be deemed to have expired or terminated' until transfer assistance is complete, which cannot be squared with a Term that ends on expiration or termination under Section 3.1.

The list 'shall include, without limitation, ISPs, fiber companies, cable TV companies ...' is a general term followed by specifics, and the closing qualifier 'receiving Wholesale Service from the Network Operator' may or may not limit every listed category.
'lit transmission service of not less than 10 Gbps to an institutional customer without protocol' uses 'without protocol' and 'institutional customer', neither of which has any settled meaning here.

Limb (c) covers institutional customers who are not Third Party Service Providers, which sits awkwardly with Section 4.8's bar on the Operator providing retail service and with Section 2.66's list of Wholesale Customers.
